CLARK COUNTY                                                                                 GUIDANCE MEMORANDUM
Comprehensive Planning Department                                                                       CP-PW-GM-2025-04
Department of Public Works — Development Review                                                               March 2025

500 S. Grand Central Parkway
Las Vegas, Nevada 89155


          Shade and Canopy Guidance for New Residential Development
Subject:            Shade and Canopy Guidance for New Residential Development
Reference No.:      CP-PW-GM-2025-04
Issued:             March 2025
Applicability:      Tentative maps, improvement plans, and landscape plans for new single-family and multi-family
                    residential subdivisions in unincorporated Clark County
Supersedes:         None

 1. Purpose
 The Southern Nevada valley continues to experience rising summer maximum temperatures and elongated
 warm-season nights, with the highest surface temperatures concentrated on hard-scape elements — asphalt drive
 lanes, concrete curb-and-gutter, sidewalks, driveways, and roof surfaces — of new residential subdivisions. The
 peer-reviewed literature and the National Weather Service Las Vegas office data both indicate that mature tree
 canopy is the single most effective site-scale mitigation measure available to reduce afternoon and evening pavement
 surface temperatures within a residential streetscape.
 The purpose of this guidance is to describe how Clark County Comprehensive Planning and Public Works evaluate
 street tree, canopy, and shade coverage during the review of tentative maps, improvement plans, and landscape
 submittals for new residential development. The guidance consolidates existing Title 30 landscape requirements with
 the shade-coverage performance target used by staff during review, so that applicants and their design consultants
 can plan streetscape landscape at the earliest possible stage.
 This memorandum does not create new law or amend Title 30. It restates the applicable code standards and describes
 how staff apply them.

 2. Applicable Standard
 The binding street frontage tree standard for new residential development is set out in Clark County Code Title 30,
 Chapter 30.64, sec. 30.64.030(k). It reads, in relevant part:
         “Large canopy trees, one (1) per thirty (30) linear feet; medium canopy trees, one (1) per
         twenty (20) linear feet; small canopy trees, one (1) per ten (10) linear feet.”
 This streetscape palette is medium canopy class, so 1 tree per 20 linear feet of street frontage applies.
 The measurement is taken along the property line abutting each public or private street. Corner lots, and
 knuckles are measured along the actual property line, following the curvature of the frontage. Fractional
 lengths are rounded up to the nearest whole tree, and where more than one frontage exists, each is summed.
 The applicant is responsible for showing the linear-foot tabulation and the resulting required tree count on the
 landscape plan cover sheet or a dedicated tabulation sheet. Staff will verify the linear-foot measurement against the
 recorded or proposed final map geometry.
 Species selection shall conform to the current Clark County / SNWA Regional Plant List. Understory and shrub
 massing are covered separately under sec. 30.64.040 and are not the subject of this memorandum.




Clark County Guidance Memorandum CP-PW-GM-2025-04 • Shade and Canopy Guidance for New Residential Development     Page 1
  3. Shade Coverage Target
 In addition to the numerical tree standard in section 2 above, staff apply a shade coverage performance target of
 30% of the streetscape area at 15-year canopy during review of new residential subdivisions.
 The target is applied as follows:

 bullet Streetscape area is defined as the horizontal projected area between the back of curb on each side of the
          street and a line parallel to and five (5) feet beyond the back of sidewalk (or, where no sidewalk is proposed,
          beyond the back of the right-of-way).
 bullet 15-year canopy is the projected horizontal canopy diameter of each proposed tree species at fifteen (15)
          years after planting, taken from the SNWA Regional Plant List canopy tables or, if the species is not listed
          there, from a source acceptable to the Comprehensive Planning Department.
 bullet 30% is the ratio, expressed as a percentage, of aggregate 15-year canopy area to streetscape area.
 The applicant demonstrates compliance through a Shade Coverage Exhibit — a single landscape sheet or overlay that
 shows each proposed tree with its 15-year canopy circle drawn to scale and overlaid on the streetscape area, together
 with a tabulation of canopy area, streetscape area, and the resulting ratio.
 Where the 30% shade coverage target cannot be met using the minimum tree count set by section 2 above — for
 example, on narrow frontages with small-stature species — the applicant is expected either to add trees beyond the
 minimum required by Chapter 30.64, or to substitute higher-canopy species, or both. The 30% target is a
 performance measure applied in addition to, not in lieu of, the numerical standard.

 4. Alternative Standards
 Chapter 30.64 provides an Alternative Standards mechanism at sec. 30.64.050 (Alternative Standards). Under sec.
 30.64.050, the applicant may propose alternative tree and landscape standards where site conditions warrant, subject
 to approval by the Comprehensive Planning Department. Typical bases for an Alternative Standards proposal
 include:

 bullet Overhead utility conflicts that preclude standard-form canopy trees along one or more frontages;
 bullet Sight-distance triangles at intersections and driveways where canopy trees would impair traffic visibility;
 bullet Subsurface conflicts (utility corridors, storm drain, dry utility joint trench) that preclude tree pit locations;
 bullet Narrow or irregular frontage geometry that cannot mathematically accommodate the standard spacing;
 bullet Substitution of higher-canopy species at wider spacing where the substitution provides equivalent or
          superior shade coverage.
 An Alternative Standards proposal shall be submitted in writing, shall identify the specific standard the applicant
 proposes to modify, shall state the reason the standard cannot be met as written, and shall describe the alternative
 treatment proposed and the equivalency basis on which the applicant asks the Department to accept it.
 Comprehensive Planning approval of an Alternative Standards proposal is discretionary and is documented in
 writing.
 Scope of the Alternative Standards mechanism. The Alternative Standards provision of sec. 30.64.050 applies to
 tree and landscape standards — spacing, species, canopy substitution, planter geometry, and comparable
 requirements within Chapter 30.64. The Alternative Standards mechanism is expressly not available to modify or
 waive the turf restrictions of sec. 30.64.030(j). Section 30.64.030(j) states, in terms, that its turf restrictions cannot
 be waived or varied. Staff will not accept, and cannot approve, an Alternative Standards proposal that seeks to
 introduce turf into a streetscape, median, or other location prohibited by sec. 30.64.030(j), or that seeks to relax the
 setback of turf from streets or curbs established by that subsection. Applicants proposing turf features in HOA
 common areas should confirm, before submittal, that the proposed turf meets a functional turf definition and is
 placed in a location permitted by sec. 30.64.030(j); the Alternative Standards route does not provide a workaround.



Clark County Guidance Memorandum CP-PW-GM-2025-04 • Shade and Canopy Guidance for New Residential Development          Page 2
  5. Coordination with SNWA Nonfunctional Turf Conversion
 The requirements described above are complementary to, and shall be read together with, the Southern Nevada
 Water Authority nonfunctional turf conversion program adopted pursuant to Nevada AB 356 (2021). Nonfunctional
 turf on property served by SNWA member agencies must be removed by the statutory compliance deadline;
 functional turf categories (playground turf within a designated play area with amenities, and athletic-field turf
 meeting minimum area and dimension thresholds) are defined by SNWA and are the operative test for whether a turf
 area is subject to conversion.
 Adding tree canopy is generally consistent with, and often supports, nonfunctional turf conversion. Converted areas
 within streetscapes and common areas can be replanted with drip-irrigated desert species and canopy trees selected
 from the Regional Plant List, producing a net reduction in landscape irrigation demand and a net increase in shade
 coverage.
 Applicants preparing a landscape submittal for a new residential subdivision are encouraged to:

 1.        Coordinate the streetscape planting palette with the SNWA nonfunctional turf conversion program at the
           earliest available stage, so that the palette submitted to Comprehensive Planning is consistent with the
           palette that will be maintained by the HOA after buildout.
 2.        Confirm that any turf feature proposed within an HOA common-area park meets a functional turf definition
           (playground or athletic) and is placed in a location permitted by sec. 30.64.030(j).
 3.        Prepare the Shade Coverage Exhibit described in section 3 concurrently with the plant schedule, so that
           species selection and tree count can be adjusted before the plans are locked in for agency review.
 4.        Where irrigation demand calculations are required by staff comment, present the calculation using the
           delivery-method rates from the SNWA irrigation demand methodology (spray-irrigated turf and
           drip-irrigated desert planting are computed separately; per-tree allowances are added for canopy trees) so
           that the effect of a palette change on total demand is transparent.


 6. Submittal Notes
 Applicants should include the following on the landscape cover sheet or a dedicated tabulation sheet at first
 submittal:

 bullet Total linear feet of street frontage, by frontage.
 bullet Required tree count per frontage under sec. 30.64.030(k) at the applicable canopy tier.
 bullet Trees shown per frontage, keyed to the plant schedule.
 bullet Streetscape area, aggregate 15-year canopy area, and the 30% shade coverage ratio.
 bullet If an Alternative Standards approach is proposed under sec. 30.64.050, a narrative describing the alternative
          and the basis for approval.
 bullet Note on the cover sheet confirming that turf, if any, is located only in areas permitted by sec. 30.64.030(j)
          and meets a functional turf definition.
 Questions on the application of this guidance may be directed to the Comprehensive Planning Department landscape
 reviewer of record, or to the Public Works Development Review civil plans examiner assigned to the project.


 Issued jointly by:

31 | Normal | An Alternative Standards request under CC 30.64.050 remains available for genuine geometry or utility conflicts, but it is discretionary, it requires a written submittal and a written Department approval, and the guidance is explicit that it "is expressly not available to modify or waive the turf restrictions of sec. 30.64.030(j)." It is a tool for tree spacing, not a route around the turf question.
32 | Heading 1 | 4.  The turf question — why the 10/20 memorandum does not close L-2
33 | Normal | Adrienne Vogel's memorandum of 10/20/2026 concludes that the nonfunctional turf prohibition does not apply to Phase 3 because the property is zoned R-2 detached and is mapped single-family residential, and asks us to adopt that position in the response matrix and record L-2 as closed. We are not able to do that, and we would be doing Callaway no service by sealing a landscape sheet that says so.
34 | Normal | The administering agency's own compliance bulletin — SNWA WRC-2024-07, which supersedes WRC-2022-04 and carries the 12/31/2026 compliance deadline — addresses the point directly. It applies to "all properties within the SNWA service area other than individually-owned single-family residential lots," and then closes the door on the project-level reading:
35 | Normal | "The single-family residential carve-out is lot-based, not project-based."
36 | Normal | "HOA-owned or HOA-managed common-area parcels of any description, including but not limited to park parcels, tot lots, greenbelts, drainage tracts, entry features, monument islands, and landscape maintenance strips" remain "fully subject to the prohibition even where they lie within a subdivision the zoning of which is single-family residential."
37 | Normal | "the presence of a single-family residential zoning designation on the underlying parcel does not confer the carve-out on common-area turf within that parcel; the operative distinction is the lot line, not the zoning district."
38 | Normal | The Parcel A park is an HOA-owned, HOA-maintained common-area parcel. Under the bulletin it is squarely inside the prohibition, and the R-2 designation does not move it out.
39 | Normal | On the functional categories, our own tabulation decides the question against us. It records 0 square feet of Phase 3 turf "within a designated play area with playground amenities." The playground equipment — slides, swings and climbing structures — was value-engineered out in July 2026 — our coordination email of 28 July 2026 records the cut — and Sheet L-3 now describes the park as "a passive-use turf lawn." Bulletin §3.1 requires amenities that are "installed and operable" and states that "a designated play area lacking installed playground amenities does not qualify as playground turf, regardless of the sign or plan label attached to the area." §4 adds that such an area "cannot be waived under Section 3.1 by promising future amenities," and that "a lawn intended for passive use, decorative purpose, aesthetic frontage, or general open space cannot be waived under Section 3.2 by asserting occasional recreational use."
40 | Normal | The contrast with Phase 1 and 2 is the tell. The approved 2022 set carried 4,200 square feet of turf "within a clearly designated play area" with slides, swings and climbing structures installed, and its compliance note said so. Phase 3 carries 18,400 square feet — more than four times as much — with none of the qualifying elements. The 18,400 square feet of cool-season sod at Parcel A constitutes nonfunctional turf, and its conversion deadline is 12/31/2026.
41 | Normal | There is a further point that forecloses the "we will deal with it when we build" fallback. The bulletin states that on and after 12/31/2026 "the presence of nonfunctional turf on a property subject to the prohibition constitutes a continuing violation." Installing new nonfunctional turf after the deadline is not a lawful alternative to converting existing turf; the prohibition is on the turf, not on the date it was planted. Deferring the decision to construction does not preserve the option.
42 | Normal | What we will put on the sheet. We will answer L-2 with the classification tabulation the County asked for — area, category and configuration for each turf hydrozone — rather than with a legal conclusion. If Ms. Vogel wishes to preserve her position, the place for it is a separate counsel letter accompanying the resubmittal, and we will include one if she authors it. What we cannot do is seal a compliance note that asserts an exemption the administering agency's own bulletin rejects: that exposes Bea Cortland's seal, the County will repeat the comment in the second round, and it leaves a recorded park that is in violation on the day it is built. A counsel letter preserves the argument; a sealed sheet does not.
43 | Normal | The association. Sagebrook wrote on 10/17/2026 asking whether Phase 3 will carry the Phase 1/2 playground amenities, and has told us that a group of homeowners will address the Phase 3 park at the 11/18/2026 TAB public comment. The letter also puts a number on delay: at the $2.85 per square foot the association has been quoted for turf-to-desert conversion, the 18,400 square feet would cost about $52,440 to convert later, after it is built and while the HOA owns it. Deleting it now avoids that cost and avoids handing the association a conversion obligation in its first reserve cycle. We recommend taking up Sagebrook's offer of a joint working session before 11/18 — the amenity question and the turf question are related, and it is better answered with the association in the room than at a public hearing.
44 | Heading 1 | 5.  The process gate: Condition 14 design review
45 | Normal | Condition 14 of the TM-22-500041 approval is not discretionary language, and it is the gate that makes a 2026 recordation impossible regardless of how fast we work:
46 | Normal | "Any significant change to approved plans, including but not limited to landscape and streetscape treatments in common areas, shall be subject to design review as a public hearing before the applicable Town Advisory Board and Planning Commission prior to staff-level action."
47 | Normal | Deleting 18,400 square feet of park lawn and adding 150 street trees to the common-area streetscape is a significant change to approved landscape and streetscape treatment in common areas. Advisory comment A-3 in the County's letter says the same thing: a revision that "materially changes the approved plan character may require additional process steps before plan approval can proceed." There is no version of the L-2/L-4 response that avoids this — even Option A, which deletes rather than adds, changes the approved park character.
48 | Normal | Design review cannot conclude before 12/23/2026, and that is true even if the County were to complete its second-round review instantly. The Board's recommendation on 12/16 must be followed by a Planning Commission hearing and action; staff cannot take action before that; and the County's 20-business-day second-round review clock runs from receipt of the complete 11/30 resubmittal, not from the end of design review. The landscape revision and the statutory deadline are therefore not in series — they conflict.
49 | Normal | We also cannot keep the item off the TAB calendar. The association has said its members will attend on 11/18 regardless, and a public hearing we did not request is worse for Callaway than one we did: without an application there is no staff report, no applicant presentation and no record of our position, and Mr. Yeoman still cannot act on the sheets. Filing on 11/25 is the only way to have our own record before the Board in December.
50 | Heading 1 | 6.  What has to happen first — and what we can commit to
51 | Normal | The sequence below is the shortest one that produces a package the County can act on and Bea Cortland can seal. Every date is a working date; the 11/30 entry is the one that matters commercially, and it holds only if the 11/06 and 11/10 decisions are in writing. We will also state on the transmittal, in the response matrix and in a cover note to Mr. Yeoman that the landscape sheets are submitted pending Condition 14 design review — we are not going to file this package as though that review were behind us.
52 | Heading 2 | 6.1  Gates that are not landscape, and that we have been treating as though they were closed
53 | Normal | •   The CCWRD capacity confirmation has already expired. Confirmation CCWRD-SCC-2025-1187 was issued 09/30/2025 for one year and "expires on 09/30/2026." The District's terms are that "[r]enewal must be requested in writing prior to expiration; expired confirmations require re-review of downstream conditions and reissuance before plan approval," and Condition 22 requires the confirmation to be current at final map recordation. We are 31 days past expiry as of this memorandum. A renewal request should go out on 11/02; the District's re-review time is outside our control and we should not assume it is short.
54 | Normal | •   The title report runs out on 01/01/2027. Report SBT-2026-04188 is effective 07/01/2026 and satisfies the six-month currency test in comment M-4 for an 11/30/2026 resubmittal. It will have to be updated for a Q1 2027 recordation — another reason not to represent this as a December closing.
55 | Normal | •   The bond has to move with the estimate. Condition 8 requires security "in the full amount of the engineer's estimate of probable cost," and Advisory comment A-6 reminds us that the estimate "forms the basis of the performance security." The 10/10/2026 sealed estimate changes under any of the three turf options (see §8). It must be re-sealed by Mr. Kessler, and the SIA and bond amount revised, before recordation.
56 | Normal | •   The Owner's Certificate still needs a signatory. Comment M-5 requires the current authorized signatory for Callaway Land Partners in the Nevada statutory notary form. The 2024 map was executed before Karen L. Montoya, whose commission runs to 01/31/2027, so the same notary is available if you sign again. We need written confirmation by 11/13.
57 | Normal | •   The water will-serve is not a constraint. LVVWD letter LVVWD-WS-2026-3341 dated 07/22/2026 runs to 07/22/2028 — but note that it also binds the project to the District's conservation rules "including limitations on turf and landscape irrigation," which is another reason the turf answer has to be right rather than asserted.
58 | Normal | If the 11/06 decisions slip, 11/30 slips with them. A one-week slip in the decisions moves the resubmittal to 12/07/2026, which leaves 12 business days before the statutory date — fewer than the County needs for second-round review alone. At that point the extension application stops being a contingency and becomes the plan.
59 | Heading 1 | 7.  Decisions we need from Callaway
60 | Normal | Five decisions, each with a date. The consequence of silence is listed because on this schedule silence is itself a decision.
61 | Heading 1 | 8.  Cost, fee and bond

cc: Mr. Max Braddock, PM — Sundial Engineering & Survey

Re: Desert Sage Ranch HOA — Phase 3 Park Landscape and Nonfunctional Turf Conversion
Cost

Dear Garrett,

Thank you for the update at last week’s coordination call and for keeping our office in the loop as the Phase
3 improvement plans and final map move through their current review cycle. The Phase 1/2 Board and the
homeowners we work with share Callaway’s interest in a smooth recordation, and this letter is offered in
that spirit — as an early flag on a couple of items the Board would like to have addressed before Phase 3
crosses the counter, so that questions from the community do not surface at a less convenient moment.

Nonfunctional turf conversion — Phase 1/2 common areas. The Board reviewed the Southern Nevada
Water Authority nonfunctional turf compliance materials at its October regular meeting and has taken
counsel from our office and from a landscape contractor on what the 12/31/2026 deadline means for the
association. Our understanding, and the advice we have been given, is that any turf conversion required in
the existing Phase 1/2 common areas — parcels the association owns and maintains — is a cost that falls to
the association rather than to the developer, and the Board has begun budgeting on that basis. Current
pricing we have collected from two local contractors for turf-to-desert conversion in park settings runs on
the order of $2.85 per square foot, inclusive of removal, soil prep, drip retrofit, decomposed granite, and a
modest planting palette. Even the areas the Board expects to keep as functional playground turf still leave a
scope that, when combined with adjacent landscape refresh the community has been discussing, is projected
to reach into the tens of thousands of dollars for the association in the next reserve cycle. The Board is
prepared to absorb its share of that obligation. It has, however, asked me to make sure the developer’s team
is aware that the community is watching how the Phase 3 landscape reads against the same standard.

Phase 3 park — playground amenities. The Board’s second and more forward-looking question concerns
the Phase 3 park. On the current landscape sheets circulated at the September coordination meeting, the
Phase 3 park parcel reads to us as a turfed lawn without the play equipment the Phase 1/2 park carries. The
Phase 1/2 park was built with slides, swings, and climbing structures inside a bordered play area, and in
every homeowner survey we have run since 2024 that playground has come up as one of the two or three
most-used common-area amenities in the community — ahead of the trail loop and the ramada, and
comparable to the pool. Families with children moved to Desert Sage Ranch in part because of it.

We are asking, plainly, whether the Phase 3 park will include the same playground amenities — slides,
swings, and climbing structures within a designated play area — as the Phase 1/2 park. The Board would
like to be able to tell homeowners that the answer is yes. If the current design does not carry those amenities
 forward, the Board would appreciate the opportunity to sit down with your landscape architect and Mr.
Braddock’s team before the resubmittal is finalized, to understand the reasoning and to discuss whether there
is room to reintroduce them. We recognize that the two questions above are related in ways that the Board
does not need to spell out here; the design team will see them, and we trust the design team to weigh them.

Enterprise Town Advisory Board — 11/18/2026. In the interest of transparency, and so this does not come
as a surprise: a group of Phase 1/2 homeowners has organized to attend the Enterprise Town Advisory Board
meeting on 11/18/2026 and to address the Phase 3 park treatment during public comment. They intend to
speak respectfully and to focus on the amenity question rather than on personalities or on Callaway’s
broader entitlement, but they will speak, and the local paper occasionally covers TAB comment. The Board
has not endorsed any particular position for the homeowners to take; it has, however, declined to discourage
them from attending. I mention it now, rather than the week before, so that the Callaway team and Sundial
have time to consider whether an outreach conversation ahead of that meeting would be useful.

Offer to coordinate. Our office is available to host a joint working session at the Sagebrook offices in the
next two to three weeks, at whatever time suits Callaway and Sundial, with the Phase 1/2 Board president
and our landscape committee chair present. If it would help, I can also circulate the homeowner survey
results and the two contractor quotes referenced above in advance of any such meeting, so that the numbers
we are working from are in front of everyone. Please let me know how you would like to proceed. I remain
the point of contact for the association on this matter and am reachable at the direct line and email below.

Thank you again for your continued attention to the community as Desert Sage Ranch completes its final
phase. The Board’s goal, and mine, is a Phase 3 that feels of a piece with what is already built — for the new
homeowners as well as for the ones already here.

Sincerely,


Ruthann Meeker

    Construction Standards. Improvement plans must be submitted to the District’s Engineering Services group for

    Plumbing Code, the Nevada Administrative Code, and the District’s Cross-Connection Control Program, including

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

Landscape improvements for Phase 1 and Phase 2 of the Desert Sage Ranch subdivision, including public
street frontage landscape strips along Windmill Ln. and the interior collector, the two entry monument treatments
at Rainbow Blvd. and at the interior collector, and the HOA common-area park at Lot A of Phase 2. Turf is
provided only within the designated play area at the common-area park, in conjunction with playground
amenities, as detailed on Sheet L-3. No turf is proposed in streetscapes, medians, entry treatments, or any
location within ten feet of a street or curb.
 GENERAL LANDSCAPE NOTES

    All work shall conform to Clark County Code Title 30, Chapter 30.64 (Landscaping, Walls and Buffers), the
    Southern Nevada Regional Plant List, and the Clark County Standard Drawings current at the date of
    approval.
    Turf placement complies with Clark County Code sec. 30.64.030(j), which permits turf in conjunction with
    cemeteries, parks and schools and prohibits turf within ten feet of a street or curb. Restrictions of sec.
    30.64.030(j) may not be waived or varied and have been observed throughout.
    Turf within the HOA common-area park is provided only within the designated play area at Lot A, in
    conjunction with the playground amenities called out on Sheet L-3 (slides, swings, and climbing structures),
    and qualifies as functional playground turf under the SNWA Regional Plant List and functional turf
    definitions.
    Streetscape planting is limited to drip-irrigated, desert-adapted species listed on the Southern Nevada
    Regional Plant List.
    All planted areas shall be irrigated by an automatic controller with rain-sensor lockout. Turf areas shall be
    spray-irrigated on a dedicated station; all other planted areas shall be drip-irrigated on separate stations.
    Street tree spacing shall meet the Clark County canopy standard of one tree per twenty linear feet of street
    frontage, measured continuously along each dedicated right-of-way.
    Minimum tree size at installation: 24-inch box, single-trunk, with a minimum caliper of 1.5 inches measured
    six inches above finish grade.
    All planting pits shall be excavated to twice the width and one-and-one-half times the depth of the root ball.
    Backfill shall be native soil amended with organic material at a rate of one part amendment to three parts
    native soil.
    A three-inch layer of decomposed granite mulch (¾-inch minus, tan) shall be provided over all planted areas
    outside the play area. Wood or bark mulches are not permitted.
    All landscape shall be maintained by the subdivider until the association is formed. Common-area
    maintenance boundaries will be established by the declaration of covenants and are not repeated on these
    sheets.
    Contractor shall verify all existing utility locations prior to excavation and shall not plant trees within any
    dedicated utility easement without written permission of the utility.
    The landscape architect of record for these sheets is Bea Cortland, PLA, NV LA #742, Ocotillo Landscape
    Studio.

SUNDIAL ENGINEERING & SURVEY

Civil Engineering · Land Surveying · Land Planning

4720 South Rainbow Boulevard, Suite 210 · Las Vegas, Nevada 89103 · (702) 555-0142 · NV COA #C-3874

MEMORANDUM

| To | Garrett Nokes, Vice President — Land Development, Callaway Land Partners |
|---|---|
| From | Max Braddock, Project Manager, Sundial Engineering & Survey |
| Cc | Adrienne Vogel, Esq., Vogel & Marsh LLP Jonathan R. Kessler, PE, Principal-in-Charge, Sundial Engineering & Survey |

| Re | Desert Sage Ranch Phase 3 — the L-series street tree and turf revision: can Sundial commit to the 11/30/2026 resubmittal and the 12/18/2026 recordation on this revision, and what has to happen first? |
| Job | 2201-03  ·  TM-22-500041 / IP-26-100288 / FM-26-100290 |
| Response requested by | Friday, November 6, 2026 |

Enclosures: Attachments A, B and C.  Basis of this memorandum: the landscape sheets L-1 through L-4 issued for plan check on 08/21/2026, the CCPW first-round comment letter of 10/09/2026, the resubmittal tracker dated 10/31/2026, and the record documents listed in Attachment C. Nothing in this memorandum has been sent to the County.


## 1.  Bottom line

No. We cannot commit Callaway to a 12/18/2026 recordation on this revision, and we should not let 11/30/2026 be represented — to the surety, the lender, the association or the County — as a date that protects the map. Four things drive that answer, and only one of them is the landscape work.

- The date that controls the map is 12/23/2026, not 12/18/2026 — and not 03/14/2026 or 03/14/2028. Phase 3 is a successive final map in the TM-22-500041 series. NRS 278.360 gives two years from the recording of the immediately preceding final map, and Phases 1 and 2 recorded on 12/23/2024 at Book 175, Page 60. Presentation of FM-26-100290 is due Wednesday, 12/23/2026. The 12/18 date is our own tracker target, five days inside the statutory date; it is a buffer, not a deadline, and the buffer is already gone.
- An 11/30/2026 resubmittal cannot produce a recordable map by 12/23/2026. CCPW states that second-round review is "generally completed within twenty (20) business days of receipt of a complete resubmittal." Twenty business days from 11/30/2026, allowing for the 12/25 holiday, is Tuesday, 12/29/2026 — six days past the statutory date and eleven days past 12/18. There are only 17 business days between 11/30 and 12/23 in total. And second-round approval is not recordation: after it come the performance security and the Subdivision Improvement Agreement, the County Surveyor, Zoning, Division of Water Resources and Health District certificate signatures, and Recorder processing — every one of them serial, and none of them started.
- L-2 and L-4 are substantive, not clerical. L-4 alone is 150 additional street trees (208 required against 58 shown), which moves the tree density from an average of 71.7 feet between trees to 20 feet — a 3.6-fold increase in planting along 4,160 linear feet — and brings with it a 30% shade-coverage exhibit, a revised plant schedule, a revised irrigation demand (3.28 acre-feet per year to 4.21, or 2.31 if the park lawn is deleted), a re-sealed engineer's estimate and a revised bond, and Condition 14 design review before TAB and the Planning Commission. L-2 cannot be answered by declaring an exemption; counsel's memorandum of 10/20/2026 does not close it (§4).
- What we can commit to. A complete, defensible package at the Development Review counter on 11/30/2026, provided the decisions in §7 reach us in writing by their due dates — 11/06/2026 for the turf option and the tree authorization, 11/10/2026 for design review; a design-review application filed 11/25/2026 for the 12/16/2026 TAB; and a realistic recordation in Q1 2027, with an extension application drafted and ready to file on 12/24/2026 as a contingency we do not recommend relying on (§6).
We are not asking to slow the job down. We are telling you that our own target sits five days inside the statutory date, that the County's review cycle alone runs six days past it, and that neither gap absorbs a missed decision. The only way to lose the map is to build a schedule that assumes the County, the bond, four certificate agencies and the Recorder all perform perfectly — on a package that still has an unresolved turf question in it.


## 2.  The date that controls the map

Four dates are circulating on this project. Only one of them is operative.

| Source in the record | Date asserted | Status |
|---|---|---|
| NRS 278.360, as quoted in the TM-22-500041 approval letter (03/14/2022) and in the Department's letter of 12/30/2024 (Marchetti) | Two years from recording of the immediately preceding final map. First map recorded 12/23/2024, Book 175, Page 60. | Operative. Presentation deadline Wednesday, 12/23/2026. |
| Curtis Hallenbeck, Comprehensive Planning — email of 10/15/2026 | "you were up on 03/14/2026" (four years from tentative approval) | Not correct. The four-year period governs the first map in the series; that map recorded 12/23/2024 and the Department's 12/30/2024 letter confirms the four-year clock "is no longer at issue." |
| Neil Petrosyan, Silver Butte Title — email of 10/26/2026 | "covered out to 03/14/2028" by a two-year extension | Not correct. No extension is of record; the 10/28/2024 application was declined as jurisdictionally premature; a statutory extension is discretionary, is available only on an application filed after the period has expired, and cannot exceed two years. A title officer's reading is not a source of statutory deadlines. |
| Our own resubmittal tracker — Milestones tab | "CONFIRM WITH PLANNING" | Open in the tracker; answered in this memorandum as 12/23/2026, subject to the Department's letterhead confirmation now requested. |

The statute, as the County quoted it in the approval letter, is unambiguous:

"A final map presented for recordation as the first map in a series must be presented to the governing body within four (4) years after the date of approval or conditional approval of the tentative map. Each successive final map in the same series must be presented within two (2) years after the date on which the immediately preceding final map is recorded. Failure to timely present a map terminates all proceedings relating to the subdivision."

Phases 1 and 2 recorded on 12/23/2024 — Book 175, Page 60, Instrument No. 20241223-0004421 — and the face of that map carries the Recorder's note. Two years from that date is 12/23/2026. The Department's own 12/30/2024 letter confirms that the four-year first-map clock "has accordingly been satisfied and is no longer at issue," and directs the applicant to "confirm the operative presentation deadline for any successive map." That is what we have done.

What we are doing about it. Ms. Marchetti asked us on 10/16/2026 to confirm the recordation date and recording reference of the first final map in the series in writing, so that she can respond on Department letterhead rather than by email. We are sending that confirmation on Monday, 2 November 2026. We are also asking her to state the successive-map deadline expressly. We expect the answer to be 12/23/2026, and we are not scheduling to any later date in the meantime. We are not relying on the title officer's 03/14/2028 reading, and the record does not support it: the 10/28/2024 application was returned as premature because the statute permits an application only after the period has expired; the extension is discretionary with the governing body; and the entitlement is not extended by anything in the file.

One practical consequence deserves to be stated plainly. If FM-26-100290 is not presented by 12/23/2026, "all proceedings relating to the subdivision" terminate, and the only route back is a written extension application filed after that date. That is a discretionary act by the governing body, not an entitlement, and it will be decided on a record that by then includes a missed deadline. It is a fallback, not a plan. The County made the same point in the first-round letter: comment M-1 directs the applicant "to schedule the recordation with adequate margin before that deadline." An 11/30 submittal built around a 12/18 target provides none — 12/18 is five days inside the statutory date, and we would have to hit it with no margin at all.

 DECLARATION OF COVENANTS, CONDITIONS, AND RESTRICTIONS
                                 FOR DESERT SAGE RANCH

                          WITH COMMON AREA MAINTENANCE EXHIBIT

THIS DECLARATION OF COVENANTS, CONDITIONS, AND RESTRICTIONS FOR DESERT SAGE RANCH
(this "Declaration") is made and executed this 23rd day of December, 2024, by CALLAWAY LAND PARTNERS,
a Nevada limited liability company, having a principal place of business at 8880 W. Sunset Road, Suite 400, Las
Vegas, NV 89148 (the "Declarant"), with reference to the facts recited below.



                                          ARTICLE I. RECITALS

A. Declarant is the owner in fee simple of certain real property situated in the unincorporated area of Clark
County, Nevada, being a portion of Section 27, Township 22 South, Range 60 East, M.D.M., Clark County,
Nevada, consisting of approximately 140.0 acres and commonly known and identified as the Desert Sage
Ranch subdivision (the "Property").

B. Declarant has caused the Property to be subdivided into three (3) sequential phases, being Phase 1, Phase
2, and Phase 3, together comprising residential lots, common-area parcels, streetscape parcels, and dedicated
public rights-of-way, all as more particularly depicted on the recorded final map(s) of the Property.

C. Concurrently with the execution and recordation of this Declaration, the First Final Map for Desert Sage
Ranch, Phases 1 and 2, being Map No. NFM-24-0118, is being recorded in the Office of the Clark County
Recorder at Book 175, Page 60 of Official Records ("First Final Map"). This Declaration is intended to be
recorded contemporaneously with, and to encumber the property depicted upon, the First Final Map, and to run
with and encumber the entire Property, including the Phase 3 remainder to be depicted on a successive final
map, upon its recordation.

D. It is the intention of Declarant to establish and impose upon the Property a general plan for the improvement,
protection, maintenance, and administration of Desert Sage Ranch as a planned residential community,
including without limitation the ownership and maintenance of certain common areas by a community
association formed for that purpose.
 E. Declarant intends that the covenants, conditions, restrictions, easements, assessments, charges, and liens
set forth below shall run with the land and be binding upon all persons or entities having or acquiring any right,
title, or interest in the Property or any portion thereof, and shall inure to the benefit of each Owner thereof.

F. Declarant has caused this Declaration to be prepared by Adrienne Vogel, Esq., of Vogel & Marsh LLP,
outside counsel to Declarant, in the manner set forth herein.

NOW, THEREFORE, Declarant hereby declares that the Property shall be held, sold, conveyed, encumbered,
hypothecated, leased, used, occupied, and improved subject to the following covenants, conditions, restrictions,
easements, assessments, charges, and liens, all of which are declared to be in furtherance of a general plan
and scheme for the subdivision, improvement, and sale of the Property.



                                          ARTICLE II. DEFINITIONS

The following capitalized terms, when used in this Declaration, shall have the meanings set forth in this Article II.
Terms not otherwise defined herein shall have the meanings customarily ascribed to them under Chapter 116 of
the Nevada Revised Statutes.

Section 2.1. "Articles." The Articles of Incorporation of the Association, as the same may be amended from
time to time.

Section 2.2. "Association." Desert Sage Ranch Community Association, a Nevada nonprofit corporation,
being the community association formed by Declarant to administer, own, and maintain the Common Area and
to enforce the terms of this Declaration. The Association is the community association contemplated by NRS
Chapter 116. All references herein to "HOA" mean the Association.

Section 2.3. "Board." The Board of Directors of the Association.

Section 2.4. "Bylaws." The Bylaws of the Association, as the same may be amended from time to time.

Section 2.5. "Common Area." All real property (including any Improvements thereon) that is (i) owned by the
Association in fee simple, or (ii) held by the Association under an easement, license, or maintenance obligation
for the common use and enjoyment of the Owners. Common Area expressly includes, without limitation, the
Common-Area Park, the Streetscape Common Area, the Entry Feature, and all landscaping, irrigation
infrastructure, hardscape, walls, monumentation, signage, and amenities located therein as installed by
Declarant or its successors. Common Area does not include any Lot or any portion of a public right-of-way
conveyed by dedication to Clark County or another public body.

Section 2.6. "Common-Area Park." The parcel of Common Area designated on the recorded final map as
Parcel A, being an active-use park parcel improved with landscaping, irrigation, and, as installed by Declarant,
any turf area and any playground amenities (which, where installed, may consist of slides, swings, and climbing
structures). Parcel A is owned by the Association and is not part of any Lot.

Section 2.7. "Declarant." Callaway Land Partners, a Nevada limited liability company, and its successors and
assigns to whom the rights of Declarant hereunder are expressly assigned in a recorded instrument.

Section 2.8. "Declaration." This Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions for Desert Sage
Ranch, together with all exhibits and attachments hereto and all amendments and supplements duly recorded.
 Section 2.9. "Entry Feature." The parcel of Common Area designated on the recorded final map as Parcel C,
being the community entry treatment situated at the intersection of Rainbow Boulevard and Windmill Lane, and
improved with entry monumentation, signage, walls, planting, irrigation, and accent lighting. Parcel C is owned
by the Association and is not part of any Lot.

Section 2.10. "Governing Documents." This Declaration, the Articles, the Bylaws, and the rules and
regulations of the Association, each as the same may be amended from time to time, together with all recorded
exhibits, plats, and supplemental declarations.

Section 2.11. "Improvement." Any structure, wall, fence, monument, sign, tree, shrub, turf, planting, irrigation
line, playground amenity, path, hardscape, or other tangible thing installed upon or affixed to the land.

Section 2.12. "Lot." Each numbered residential lot depicted upon a recorded final map of the Property and
intended for the construction and occupancy of a single detached residential dwelling. Each Lot is a separately
conveyable parcel; no Lot includes any portion of any Common Area, and no Common Area is any part of any
Lot.

Section 2.13. "Managing Agent." The community management firm engaged by the Association pursuant to a
written management agreement to perform the day-to-day administration of the Association's affairs, including
the maintenance and replacement obligations set forth in Article V. As of the date of this Declaration, the
Managing Agent is Sagebrook Community Management LLC, a Nevada limited-liability company, having offices
at 6280 S. Pecos Road, Suite 300, Las Vegas, NV 89120.

Section 2.14. "Map" or "Final Map." Any final subdivision map of any portion of the Property recorded in the
Office of the Clark County Recorder, including the First Final Map (Map No. NFM-24-0118, recorded at Book
175, Page 60) and any successive final map for Phase 3.

Section 2.15. "Owner." The record holder of fee simple title to a Lot, excluding any person or entity holding title
solely as security for the performance of an obligation.

Section 2.16. "Property." All of the real property described in Article III below and shown upon the Map(s),
together with all Improvements thereon, and any additional property annexed hereto in accordance with this
Declaration.

Section 2.17. "Streetscape Common Area." Those parcels or strips of Common Area situated between the
back-of-curb of a public street and the front or side lot lines of the adjoining Lots (or, where applicable, between
the back-of-curb and a perimeter community wall), extending along all frontage of the Property, and improved
with sidewalks (where the sidewalk is not within the dedicated public right-of-way), desert planting, street trees,
and drip irrigation. Each Streetscape Common Area parcel is owned by the Association and is not part of any
Lot.



                                ARTICLE III. PROPERTY DESCRIPTION

Section 3.1. Legal Description of the Property. The Property subject to this Declaration is that certain real
property situated in the unincorporated area of Clark County, State of Nevada, more particularly described as
follows:

       A portion of Section 27, Township 22 South, Range 60 East, M.D.M., Clark County, Nevada,
       containing approximately 140.0 acres, together with all easements, tenements, hereditaments, and
       appurtenances thereunto belonging, commonly known as Desert Sage Ranch, situated at the
       intersection of Rainbow Boulevard and Windmill Lane, Las Vegas, Nevada 89178.
 Section 3.2. Phasing. The Property is subject to development in three sequential phases:

(a) Phase 1 — as more particularly depicted upon the First Final Map (Map No. NFM-24-0118, Book 175, Page
60), consisting of residential Lots, streetscape and open-space Common Area, and dedicated street
rights-of-way, all as shown upon Sheets 2 through 4 of the First Final Map.

(b) Phase 2 — as more particularly depicted upon the First Final Map (Map No. NFM-24-0118, Book 175, Page
60), consisting of residential Lots, streetscape and open-space Common Area (including the Common-Area
Park designated Parcel A, the shared Detention Facility designated Parcel B, and the Entry Feature designated
Parcel C), and dedicated street rights-of-way, all as shown upon Sheets 2 through 4 of the First Final Map.

(c) Phase 3 — that portion of the Property consisting of approximately 40.0 acres, presently identified by Clark
County Assessor's Parcel Number 177-27-201-001, to be subdivided into approximately sixty (60) half-acre
residential Lots, together with associated streetscape Common Area and dedicated street rights-of-way, all to be
depicted upon a successive final map to be recorded by Declarant. Upon recordation of the Phase 3 final map,
the Lots and Common Area created thereby shall automatically be and become subject to this Declaration
without the necessity of any further instrument.

Section 3.3. Annexation of Successive Phases. Declarant reserves the right, exercisable in its sole discretion
and without the consent of any Owner, Mortgagee, or the Association, to annex Phase 3 (and any lawful
reconfiguration thereof) to the regime of this Declaration by recordation of a Supplemental Declaration in the
Office of the Clark County Recorder that (i) identifies the annexed property by reference to the recorded final
map, and (ii) states that the annexed property is thereby made subject to this Declaration.

Section 3.4. Public Rights-of-Way. All streets, alleys, and other public rights-of-way depicted upon any Map
are conveyed by dedication to Clark County or the applicable public body. No such dedicated area is Common
Area, and the Association bears no maintenance obligation for improvements accepted for public maintenance
within any such dedicated area, except as provided by written agreement with the applicable public body.



                                     ARTICLE IV. COMMON AREAS

Section 4.1. Establishment of Common Area. Declarant hereby establishes and dedicates for the common
use and enjoyment of the Owners, and conveys to the Association concurrently herewith and by the recordation
of each applicable Map, all Common Area, in fee simple, free and clear of all monetary encumbrances other
than the lien of current taxes and assessments not yet delinquent and matters of record specifically noted upon
the Map.

Section 4.2. Parcel A — Common-Area Park. The parcel designated Parcel A on the First Final Map (and as
reflected in Exhibit B hereto) is hereby established as the Common-Area Park. Parcel A is owned in fee simple
by the Association and is not part of any Lot. Parcel A is improved by Declarant with landscaping, irrigation, and,
as installed by Declarant, any turf area and any playground amenities (which, where installed by Declarant, may
consist of slides, swings, and climbing structures). All landscaping, irrigation infrastructure, turf, planting,
hardscape, and playground amenities installed upon Parcel A, as and where installed, constitute Common Area
Improvements owned by the Association.

Section 4.3. Parcel C — Entry Feature. The parcel designated Parcel C on the First Final Map (and as

08/07/2026 — Weekly Project Meeting #01
Attendees
Max Braddock, Priya Sarwal — Sundial
Garrett Nokes, Lee Chastain — Callaway Land Partners
Discussion

Sundial walked through the Phase 3 submittal package status: improvement plans (C-1 through C-9) at ~90% complete; landscape (L-1 through L-4) at ~85% and in review with Ocotillo; final map ready for sign-off following one last check by the survey group.
Priya confirmed the QA/QC checklist will run the week of 08/17. Garrett asked for the target submittal date. Sundial committed to 08/21/2026.
Callaway noted that Vogel & Marsh is reviewing a memo on the single-family exemption question raised during landscape coordination. Garrett expects it to close the turf conversation.
Ocotillo's water budget worksheet and turf/planting tabulation to accompany the submittal.

MB to circulate submittal checklist and cover memo — due 08/14.
Priya to finalize C-4 through C-7 grading revisions — due 08/17.
Garrett to forward Vogel & Marsh memo to Sundial when received.
MB to confirm submittal transmittal package with the County records desk.
Next Meeting: 08/14/2026
08/14/2026 — Weekly Project Meeting #02
Attendees
Max Braddock, Priya Sarwal — Sundial
Garrett Nokes, Lee Chastain — Callaway
Bea Cortland — Ocotillo Landscape Studio (invited for landscape items)
Discussion
One week to submittal. QA/QC checklist run in progress; Priya reported cross-reference checks between plan and profile complete for C-8. Base file verified against the tentative map exhibit for horizontal control.
Bea confirmed L-1 through L-4 are ready. Plant schedule shows 58 trees along the street frontages. Common-area park is drawn with 18,400 sf of turf carried forward from the Phase 1/2 palette. Cover-sheet compliance note references the single-family carve-out per counsel.
Garrett forwarded the Vogel & Marsh email during the meeting. Adrienne Vogel's position: because Phase 3 is zoned and mapped as single-family residential, the nonfunctional turf prohibition does not apply and no turf is subject to conversion. Callaway takes this as closing the issue for submittal purposes.
Sewer capacity confirmation, water will-serve, geotech report, traffic impact statement, and dry utility composite all confirmed in the package.
Engineer's estimate of probable cost tracking to roughly $4.86M based on the County unit cost schedule. Garrett asked that it be finalized before the November bond conversation.
Action Items
Bea to deliver final L-1 through L-4 PDFs to Sundial — due 08/18.
MB to finalize submittal transmittal and clearance log — due 08/20.
Priya to complete final QA/QC sign-off — due 08/20.
Callaway to file cover letter and application fees on submittal day.
Next Meeting: 08/21/2026

from docx import Document
from docx.table import Table
from docx.text.paragraph import Paragraph
from docx.oxml.ns import qn

doc=Document('Callaway_L-Series_Turf_and_Schedule_Memo_2026-10-31.docx')
def iter_block(parent):
    body=parent.element.body
    for child in body.iterchildren():
        if child.tag==qn('w:p'): yield Paragraph(child,parent)
        elif child.tag==qn('w:tbl'): yield Table(child,parent)

out=[]
out.append('# Callaway L-Series Turf and Schedule Memorandum — final text\n')
out.append('*Transcription of `Callaway_L-Series_Turf_and_Schedule_Memo_2026-10-31.docx` as issued. '
           'Generated directly from the DOCX so that the markdown, the DOCX and the PDF carry identical text. '
           'Formatting, letterhead and page furniture are omitted; nothing else is.*\n')
out.append('---\n')
for b in iter_block(doc):
    if isinstance(b, Paragraph):
        t=b.text.strip()
        if not t: continue
        style=b.style.name if b.style is not None else ''
        if style.startswith('Heading 1'):
            out.append('\n## '+t+'\n')
        elif style.startswith('Heading 2'):
            out.append('\n### '+t+'\n')
        elif t.startswith('\u2022'):
            out.append('- '+t.lstrip('\u2022').strip())
        else:
            out.append(t+'\n')
    else:
        rows=[[c.text.strip().replace('\n',' ') for c in r.cells] for r in b.rows]
        if not rows: continue
        hdr=rows[0]; body=rows[1:]
        out.append('| '+' | '.join(hdr)+' |')
        out.append('|'+'|'.join(['---']*len(hdr))+'|')
        for r in body:
            out.append('| '+' | '.join(r)+' |')
        out.append('')
open('drafts/Callaway_L-Series_Turf_and_Schedule_Memo_2026-10-31_DRAFT.md','w').write('\n'.join(out))
print('written', len('\n'.join(out)))

 E. Declarant intends that the covenants, conditions, restrictions, easements, assessments, charges, and liens

steps.message:
All six items are fixed and the package regenerated (DOCX → PDF → markdown, workbook, PLAN). Final state: 15 pages, zero margin violations, no literal markdown, workbook and memo in agreement, nothing outside `output/` touched.

**Deliverables (unchanged locations)**

- `output/Callaway_L-Series_Turf_and_Schedule_Memo_2026-10-31.docx` + `.pdf` — memo to Garrett Nokes (cc Vogel, Kessler), dated October 31, 2026, §§1–9, Attachments A–C.
- `output/LS-01_L-Series_Reconciliation_and_Schedule_Backup.xlsx` — five tabs; Source Register now 24 documents, Schedule tab now 24 dated rows.
- `output/drafts/Callaway_L-Series_Turf_and_Schedule_Memo_2026-10-31_DRAFT.md` — memo text extracted from the DOCX.
- `output/PLAN.md` — method, earlier corrections, and a new §8 recording this pass.

**The six fixes**

1. **Parcel designation and CC&R support.** §4 now uses the reconciled label — "Common-Area Parcel **'D'** on the final map and civil plans, called **Parcel A** on the Phase 3 landscape sheets" — and distinguishes it from the recorded declaration's Parcel A (the Phases 1/2 park). It cites CC&Rs Instrument No. 20241223-0004422, Bk 175, Pg 61, §§2.6, 3.2(c) and 3.3, and states HOA ownership/maintenance as **an obligation to be perfected on recordation** under Condition 16, not a completed conveyance. Attachment B and workbook tabs 2–3 relabelled; the CC&R added to Attachment C and to tab 5.
2. **Workbook tab 4 vs. memo.** Tab 4 now mirrors §6 row for row — separate **11/06** notice to Comprehensive Planning, **11/10** decision 3, **11/13** decision 4 — and adds the missing **12/04** decision-5 row.
3. **Irrigation rounding.** Attachment B and tab 3 show the computed totals **3.287 / 4.208 / 2.307**, the carried figures (3.28 / 4.21 / 2.31) alongside, and deltas **+0.921 / −0.980**, with a note explaining that the worksheet's 3.28 is its Summary figure (2.83 + 0.45) and that subtracting the rounded 3.28 would give +0.93 / −0.97.
4. **Attachment C estimate row.** Now lists the lines actually used — 7.02, 7.09, 7.11–7.14, 7.16, 7.17, 7.41, 7.43 — and states that 7.01 is **not** used because its 80,000 sf allowance already covers the planted footprint.
5. **§5 Planning Commission claim.** Rewritten to "**No Planning Commission hearing is scheduled, and the County's review cycle alone ends 12/29/2026.**" The §5 table carries the PC date as "not scheduled — no date appears in the record" and adds a second-round row at 12/29/2026 as the controlling blocker; the unsupported "cannot conclude before 12/23" assertion is gone.
6. **§6.1 gate list.** Added **F-1** (CCFD second access; call 11/10, due 11/22) and **G-8** (NDEP NVR100000 NOI; status 11/13, due 11/22), plus a paragraph stating the other 24 General Comments are being worked to the tracker's 11/22/2026 date and are not re-planned or vouched for here — if any slips, 11/30 slips.

**Also fixed:** a table-rendering defect found while making these edits — the DOCX helper stripped the first and last two characters of any cell opening with `**` in a bold row, which truncated the new Attachment B total. The helper now strips markers only when a cell both opens and closes with `**`; the documents were re-scanned for literal markdown (none).

**Bottom line unchanged: no — do not commit to 12/18/2026, and 11/30 cannot be represented as protecting the map.** Controlling date **12/23/2026** (two years from the 12/23/2024 recording); 11/30 + 20 business days = **12/29/2026** with only 17 business days to 12/23; L‑4 is +150 trees (208 vs 58 on 4,160 lf) on L‑2/L‑1 with Sheet L‑4 unaffected; L‑2 stays open because the 18,400 sf at Parcel D is nonfunctional turf subject to the 12/31/2026 deadline; water moves 3.287 → 4.208 ac‑ft/yr (lawn kept) or 2.307 (lawn deleted); estimate +$45,150 direct, bond to be re-sealed. Decisions 1–2 by 11/06, decision 3 by 11/10, signatory by 11/13, extension decision by 12/04; design review filed 11/25 for the 12/16 TAB; resubmit 11/30 with L‑2/L‑3 pending design review; recordation Q1 2027.
